text:
Michaela: Heads up — autotuner v0.9.4 canary is showing a regression tied to KV keying. P99 token latency +17% on canary hosts, overall throughput slightly lower.

deploy-bot: Started canary rollout for autotuner v0.9.4 -> runtime-pool-canary-3

Samir: ugh, what changed in keying?

Michaela: We added arch+seqlen bin salting to the cache key so kernel selector can pick specialized shards. The change introduced a salt version but we forgot to include a backward fallback for reads and we didn't journal salt version on persistence.

Chen: Observed metrics: cache_hit_rate: 0.98 -> 0.61 on canary traffic (10m window). Miss amplification in small prefix hotkeys.

Michaela: sample KV access log (reordered to anonymize):
```
[2026-03-18T14:12:04Z] INFO kv_lookup model=rw-llama2 key=modelA:sv2:seqlenBin3:prefixhash1234 -> MISS
[2026-03-18T14:12:04Z] INFO kv_lookup model=rw-llama2 key=modelA:sv1:seqlenBin3:prefixhash1234 -> HIT
[2026-03-18T14:12:05Z] WARN kernel_selector fallback to generic path (cache miss)
```

Michaela: In short: driver upgraded nodes see sv2-written keys but persistent store has mostly sv1 keys. Reads use sv2-only lookup, so items unfindable.

Dmitri: Do we have a reproducible script? can we emulate mismatch locally?

Michaela: yes, reproduce with stress-client: set keys with salt_v=1 then run runtime with SALT_VERSION=2. Quick repro: 
```
# write sv1 keys
python tools/kv_cli.py --model modelA --salt 1 --put --prefix test-migr
# run runtime with SALT=2 and query
python tools/serve_local.py --salt 2 --query "hello"
```

Chen: Profiling snippets from canary (aggregated):
```
before:  avg_token_time_gpu=4.2ms  p99=9.8ms   kv_hit_rate=0.98
after:   avg_token_time_gpu=4.8ms  p99=11.5ms  kv_hit_rate=0.61

KV lookup latency tail also increased because of fallback path to DB: kv_store.get(...) latency 2ms -> 8ms on miss storm.
```

Samir: Immediate mitigation idea: add a read-path fallback that tries previous salt versions (sv2 -> sv1 -> unmodified). Cheap to implement as a transient compatibility layer. Also add metric `kv_lookup_salting_fallbacks`.

Dmitri: We should avoid indefinite fallback in steady-state (adds extra lookups). Plan: 1) enable backward-fallback for reads during rollout window; 2) run background rekey migration job to materialize sv2 keys for hot prefixes; 3) after migration, flip reads to sv2-only and remove fallback.

Anna: I'll open a PR that: a) adds fallback read logic + metric b) introduces a `salt_version` header on persisted objects c) adds a migration job CLI d) sets a canary pause hook.

Michaela: For migration job we should pick top-N hot prefixes from last 24h (use route-level telemetry), rehash into new salted keyspace and write with idempotent put with `migrate=true` flag. Also keep TTL and owner metadata to avoid double-counting.

Chen: Query to get hot prefixes: `curl -s http://metrics.internal/api/series?name=route.token_count&top=200` then filter by model and prefix. We'll add a small tool that bulk-inserts keys back into kv store with target salt.

ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0318-KV-SALT-REGRESS. Pager duty not triggered.

Samir: What about persistence journaling format? if we don't embed salt_version, recovery won't know. We need to bump journal schema and add backwards-compatible decoder.

Dmitri: Agree, add a schema version byte to journal records and update loader to read both. Migration can't rely solely on fallback. Schema bump + migration job + short fallback window = low risk.

Michaela: Quick risk calc: without mitigation we'll keep missing hot prefixes and see 10-30% cost increase for short-running endpoints (extra DB lookups). With fallback + migration we expect hit-rate back to ~95% within a 2h migration for top-200 prefixes.

Anna: Action items I'm assigning to myself: PR for fallback + metrics (link coming), migration tool prototype, add canary pause toggle. Target: roll back canary pause now? prefer to pause v0.9.4 until fallback PR merged.

Michaela: Pausing canary now. deploy-bot: rollback initiated -> runtime-pool-canary-3 to v0.9.3

deploy-bot: Rollback complete (duration 45s).

Samir: nice. Anna: please attach perf dashboards and the quick repro steps to the PR. Also add an integration test that simulates mixed-salt store.

Anna: will do.

Michaela: Thanks all. We'll track `kv_lookup_salting_fallbacks`, `kv_rekey_migrated_keys`, and hit-rate metric. Post-migration we'll schedule a sweep to delete stale sv1 keys after 7 days.

Samir: :+1:

Michaela: :grimacing: (lesson: never change keyspace without a migration story)
